card.name: Waltz
card.tagline: Vienna, 1700s — once condemned as obscene for the closed embrace, now the wedding dance of the West.
card.profile: The waltz (from German Walzer [ˈvaltsɐ] , meaning "to roll or revolve") is a ballroom and folk dance, in triple ( 34 ) time, performed primarily in closed position, originating from German-speaking regions of Europe in the 18th century. Along with the ländler and allemande, the waltz was sometimes referred to by the generic term German Dance in publications during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
card.insight: The French philosopher Michel de Montaigne wrote of a dance he saw in 1580 in Augsburg, where the dancers held each other so closely that their faces touched. The ladies of Vienna are particularly celebrated for their grace and movements of waltzing of which they never tire." There is a waltz in the second act finale of the 1786 opera Una Cosa Rara by Martin y Soler.

lessons.teacher_style: The male teacher leads the explanation while the female partner demonstrates alongside him or with him. They break down steps into leader and follower roles with clear verbal cues.
lessons.distinctive_method: Breaking down every step into separate solo demonstrations for leaders and followers before putting them together in hold.
what_works: separating leader and follower footwork explanations
using visual diagrams and floor references
what_hinders: switching between couple demonstration and solo footwork quickly
